body:
### Follow-up: the same `device_synchronize` crash is reached through call paths a Python-level workaround can't cover — including from *inside* a compiled graph

I hit this exact bug (same `c10::xpu::device_synchronize → device_impl::wait → queue_impl::~queue_impl → urQueueRelease` SIGSEGV) in a real workload — vLLM's XPU **cudagraph capture** (FULL decode graphs) on the same Battlemage + `torch==2.13.0+xpu` / oneAPI 2026.0 stack. Capturing a set of 35 decode graphs, the crash fires *during capture*, not just on an explicit user `torch.xpu.synchronize()`.

When I traced it, the **same** device-level sync is reached through **three distinct entry points** during capture, all converging on the path in the original report:

1. **`torch.accelerator.synchronize()`** — Python-level; can be redirected to `current_stream().synchronize()`.
2. **`torch.xpu.empty_cache()`** → C++ `c10::xpu::XPUCachingAllocator::NativeCachingAllocator::emptyCache()` → `c10::xpu::device_synchronize()`. (vLLM calls `empty_cache()` in its capture loop.)
3. **`torch.xpu.synchronize()` invoked from *inside* a compiled (Dynamo/Inductor) graph** — `THXPModule_xpuSynchronize` via `torch::jit::invokeOperatorFromPython` under `dynamo__custom_eval_frame`. The symbol is bound at compile time, so a Python-level monkeypatch of `torch.xpu.synchronize` does **not** intercept it.

Backtrace for entry point (3):

```
... ur_loader::urQueueRelease(ur_queue_handle_t_*)
... sycl::_V1::detail::queue_impl::~queue_impl()
... sycl::_V1::detail::device_impl::wait()
... c10::xpu::device_synchronize(signed char)
... THXPModule_xpuSynchronize(_object*, _object*)
... torch::jit::invokeOperatorFromPython(...)
... dynamo__custom_eval_frame
```

**Practical consequence:** redirecting `torch.xpu.synchronize` / `torch.accelerator.synchronize` at the Python level (the workaround in the issue) is **necessary but not sufficient** for compiled workloads. Concretely, with (1) redirected and (2) no-op'd, XPU cudagraph capture progresses from **1/35 to 34/35** graphs — but (3), the in-graph `synchronize`, still SIGSEGVs on the final capture. So the bug effectively blocks XPU full-cudagraph capture on Battlemage and can't be fully papered over from Python.

This reinforces that the fix belongs in `c10::xpu::device_synchronize` itself — making device-level sync stream-safe / idempotent with respect to queues owned by an active graph (sync the relevant stream(s) rather than destroying/releasing graph-owned queue handles), so that all three call paths become safe at once.

*Same hardware/stack as the issue body. AI assistance was used to investigate and draft; the backtraces and the 1/35→34/35 capture behavior were produced and verified on real hardware.*
I think the regression bug is caused by https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/182630. I will check first and fix it soon.
Hi @TSUMUGI-XE, I have the root cause and will fix it in #187306. I think you could get this patch in the release branch as well.

Confirmed fixed on real Battlemage hardware — thanks for the fast turnaround.

I applied #187306 (the revert of #182630) and tested on an **Arc Pro B70 (BMG-G31 / Xe2)**, `torch==2.13.0+xpu` / oneAPI 2026.0. Since the change is contained in `libc10_xpu` (the removed `c10::xpu::device_synchronize` is internal — nothing in `libtorch_xpu` / `libtorch_python` / `_C` references it as undefined), I rebuilt just `libc10_xpu.so` from the `a3aa2c6` sources with the revert and dropped it in (ABI-checked: the only public symbol that disappears is `device_synchronize`; all external `c10::xpu::*` references stay satisfied).

Two checks:

1. **Minimal repro** (pure `torch.xpu` XPU-graph capture → `torch.xpu.synchronize()`): **was SIGSEGV, now passes** (capture + replay, both elementwise and matmul).

2. **Real workload — XPU full cudagraph capture in vLLM:** previously the capture loop SIGSEGV'd part-way (and a Python-level redirect of `synchronize` / `empty_cache` could only get it to 34/35 before the in-graph `synchronize` — call path (3) in my earlier comment — crashed the last graph). With the C++ revert in place, **`FULL_DECODE` cudagraph capture now completes 35/35 and the server comes up healthy**, with no Python-side workarounds enabled. Output is correct (greedy smoke returns coherent text).

So the revert closes all three entry points (`accelerator.synchronize`, `empty_cache`→`emptyCache`, and the in-graph `synchronize`) at once, exactly as expected from it routing `syncStreamsOnDevice` back through the per-owned-queue path.

As a side note, this is a meaningful unlock on Xe2, not just a correctness fix: full cudagraph replay removes the per-op host-dispatch overhead that otherwise dominates single-stream decode here. On the same image / harness / model (a 35B-A3B MoE in MXFP4), single-stream decode went **eager 10.4 → torch.compile 15.6 → torch.compile + full cudagraph 68.1 tok/s** — a ~4.4× step from enabling cudagraph alone, which lines up with single-stream decode being host-dispatch-bound on this hardware until the graph closes that gap. (It compounds with continuous batching too — aggregate decode reaches ~800 tok/s at 64-way concurrency on the single card, still climbing.)

Happy to re-verify once it's cherry-picked to the release branch; this regime won't show up on Data-Center-GPU CI, so I'm glad to keep testing it on BMG.

*AI assistance was used to investigate and verify; the repro, the 1/35 → 34/35 → 35/35 capture behavior, and the symbol/ABI checks were all run on real hardware.*
